## LLMs - overview

- Large language models are powerful autocomplete engines
- They use "tokens" ~ words
- **Training** "teaches" the LLM the probabilities of associations between tokens
- **Inference** generates a response by sequential prediction of the next token given the full context (all previous tokens)

## Training

LLM learns the probabilities of next tokens by training on a huge corpus of data

```{mermaid}

flowchart LR
    A["Input text<br/><br/>The analyst examines the"] --> B["Large language model"]
    B --> C{"Possible next tokens"}
    C --> D["data<br/>0.42"]
    C --> E["results<br/>0.31"]
    C --> F["evidence<br/>0.17"]
    C --> G["other tokens<br/>0.10"]

    classDef input fill:#E8F1FA,stroke:#2B6CB0,color:#1A202C
    classDef model fill:#E9D8FD,stroke:#6B46C1,color:#1A202C
    classDef output fill:#E6FFFA,stroke:#2C7A7B,color:#1A202C

    class A input
    class B model
    class C,D,E,F,G output


```

```{mermaid}
    C1["Context<br/><br/>What does an analyst do?"]
    C2["Context<br/><br/>What does an analyst do?<br/>An"]

    classDef input fill:#E8F1FA,stroke:#2B6CB0,color:#1A202C

```
## What LLMs can do {.smaller}


- Generate, summarise and transform text
- Extract themes and structured information from documents
- Answer questions based on the data they were trained on 
- Translate, classify and compare information
- Generate code, analysis plans and draft reports
- Adapt outputs to different audiences
- Reason about problems within the information available in the prompt


## What LLMs cannot do {.smaller}


- Access information that is not included in their training or current context
- Take actions in external systems
- Search documents, emails or databases independently
- Execute code, run analyses or interact with software tools
- Verify whether their answers are true
- Have memory between conversations
- Work autonomously on multi-step tasks over extended periods

. . .


**An agent is an LLM embedded within a system that can remember, plan, use tools and take actions to achieve a goal**

## LLMs as the conductors of agents{.smaller}

- Agents are the orchestrators
- Agents plan, choose tools, integrate results
- Only have access to the specified tools
- Tools can include LLMs


## Scaling up agents to agentic AI

- Spectrum: Agents -> Agentic
- "Agentic": autonomous actions
- Agent tools can create other agents
- Adaptive behaviour


## Agents in SG

- Copilot Premium to have agent feature
- "Researcher" , "analyst" agents
- Still black box. We do not currently have permission to create agents

## Risks

- Agents can interpret instructions in unexpected ways
- Black box of hidden "outputs" means it is difficult to know what is being passed
- Agents only have access to the tools they are given. 
- Tools to change system can introduce risks. Need oversight points included



## Environmental footprint

- Standard AI queries have ~0.3Wh
- Queries that use agentic workflows 50 -- 500Wh/workflow
